newsitem.title: USA: Massive drive to push for U.S. campaign reform.
newsitem.headline: Massive drive to push for U.S. campaign reform.

text.p: Organisers of a nationwide drive for campaign finance reform said Tuesday they plan to kick off their movement by collecting 1,776,000 signatures of support.

Common Cause, a campaign watchdog group, and Campaign For America, a group founded by financier Jerome Kohlberg, said the petitions would urge passage of campaign finance reform by the Independence Day holiday on July 4.

The groups support campaign finance reform legislation introduced by Arizona Republican Sen. John McCain and Wisconsin Democratic Sen. Russell Feingold that bans large corporate and labour "soft money" donations to parties and puts voluntary limits on spending among other reforms.
Don Simon, executive vice president of Common Cause, said the purpose of the petition drive "is to show the depth and breadth of support for campaign finance reform."

On Monday, another group seeking campaign finance reform, Citizen Action, said that the McCain-Feingold bill and other campaign finance proposals in Congress do not meet the tests of true reform and called for public financing of elections.
Simon disagreed with that criticism. "We strongly disagree because McCain-Feingold addresses all the serious problems."
Besides, he added, "public financing has no chance" in this Congress.
